title: Options grow with every branch
hook: Expand a design tree and count candidates, not their quality.

doesNotKnow: Identify how local branching multiplies candidate-search size.

misconception: Doubling local options only doubles exhaustive multi-stage search work.
objective: Identify how local branching multiplies candidate-search size.

claims.text: Design involves searching alternatives under constraints on computation and attention.
Herbert A. Simon, The Sciences of the Artificial (1969)
One option per stage creates {A} nodes; two create {B}. Extra local choices multiply later alternatives in this collision-free tree.
Does it hold up? This counts enumerated candidates only. It does not measure quality, attention, partial-design reuse or search-heuristic performance.
claims.source: {"type":"source-access-hold","note":"No empirical effect or research verdict established. Only bounded arithmetic proposed."}

recall.question: Three stages offer three independent choices each. How many complete designs?
recall.why: 3×3×3=27; total tree nodes additionally count prefixes.
